speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what proportion of resale HDB flat buyers paid Cash-Over-Valuation (COV) since 14 February 2023, when enhancements to the CPF Housing Grant were announced; (b) what is the mean and median COVs since 14 February 2023; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider making the CPF Housing Grant conditional on COVs to keep COVs prudent and sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: On 14 Februay 2023, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced that the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Housing Grant would be increased to provide more support for First-Timer Singaporeans seeking a resale flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Housing and Development Board (HDB) resale flat transactions are conducted on a "willing buyer-willing seller" basis, with prices negotiated and mutually agreed upon between flat sellers and buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Cash-Over-Valuation (COV) arises when the resale price is higher than the market valuation of the flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The CPF Housing Grant is targeted at first-timer buyers who meet income criteria and other eligibility conditions, limiting its impact on the overall resale market.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I am glad to hear that the COV situation has calmed down in the last three years.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I think it is especially important for COV to remain low and stable, especially for first-timers who are buying resale flats.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: So, in this respect, I just want to ask the Senior Minister of State whether the Ministry will be minded to consider a tiered system of haircuts to the CPF Housing Grant, pegged to different amounts of COV, to promote prudence in the determination of COV between buyer and seller.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Basically, he is asking, can we give less CPF Housing Grant if less COV is paid and perhaps even consider vice versa.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As I shared earlier in my main reply, the COV is determined between a willing buyer and a willing seller, and arises when the transacted price is above the valuation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Because it is a willing buyer-willing seller agreement, there is a high chance of it being hard to enforce because the buyer and seller could collude to circumvent the restrictions.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The second point is, as I said, it is a willing buyer-willing seller agreement.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Between the two, there are many considerations at play.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Potentially, it could be the attributes of the flat, the location possibly.
